finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: A user inputs a malicious file name that leads to command execution
finding.assumptions: The file path manipulation and existence check could lead to command injection if the file path is not properly sanitized or validated.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked the code around lines 60-67 and verified that the user-supplied string is only combined with a directory path using Path.Combine and then passed to File.Exists, which performs a file existence check without invoking any external process or OS command. No Process.Start, ShellExecute, or other command execution is present. The only potential concern would be directory traversal, but this does not lead to OS command execution and is not a command injection vulnerability.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: A user inputs a malicious directory name that leads to command execution
finding.assumptions: The directory path manipulation and file retrieval could lead to command injection if the directory path is not properly sanitized or validated.

parsed.refutation_attempt: The Directory.GetFiles call at lines 93‑95 uses a hard‑coded directory name ('Data') and a constant search pattern ('round-*.csv'). No untrusted data from Console.ReadLine() or any other external source is concatenated into these arguments. Even the earlier Console.ReadLine() (line 60) is used only to build a path for a single round file via Path.Combine and then passed to File.Exists, GenerateRandomScores, and ProcessRoundResults – none of which invoke operating‑system commands. Directory.GetFiles is a library method that does not spawn external processes, so there is no avenue for OS command injection. Therefore the reported vulnerability is not present.

finding.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
finding.trigger: A user inputs a malicious input that leads to command execution
finding.assumptions: The input parsing could lead to command injection if the input is not properly sanitized or validated.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked that the user input from Console.ReadLine() is only parsed by int.TryParse on line 43 and stored in the local variable 'choice'. No OS command is constructed or executed from this value. The switch on 'choice' merely calls internal methods; there is no dynamic invocation of external processes or use of the input in a system command. Thus the claimed OS Command Injection cannot occur. The code has no path from the input to a dangerous command execution.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: A user inputs a malicious input that leads to command execution
finding.assumptions: The input parsing and comparison could lead to command injection if the input is not properly sanitized or validated.

parsed.refutation_attempt: The code fragment only reads a string from Console.ReadLine() (line 88) and then performs a simple equality check against the literal "y" (lines 90). There is no call to any OS‐invoking API (e.g., Process.Start, System.Diagnostics.Process, exec, or any shell invocation). Therefore the input cannot be used to construct or execute an arbitrary command, so OS Command Injection is not possible here.
